title: Paired change in turn lateral RMSE
caption_en: Paired turn lateral RMSE changes: Guided MPC minus each comparison controller using matched geometry, plant, and seed. Each dot is one pair and each black bar the mean of three pairs within a geometry; negative values favor Guided MPC. All 54 paired comparisons (18 pairs against each comparator) are retained, including nominal cases where the tracker is more accurate. Pairing shares pre-generated state perturbations but does not make the native implementation bitwise deterministic. No inferential p-values or confidence intervals are shown.
manipulations: Subtract whole-trial turn RMSE values only after pairing geometry/condition/seed; mean of three pairs.

title: Angular command/body smoothness
caption_en: Angular smoothness for all tracking trials. Each dot is a whole-trial statistic; black bars are means of nine trials per method/plant. Columns distinguish raw command-increment RMS (Δu), command-rate RMS (Δu/Δt), and body-velocity second-difference RMS (Δ²v/Δt², a numerical jerk estimate). Δt=0.05 s; differences use recorded samples, no filtering and no artificial prepended zero; startup is included. Command increment has velocity units and is not acceleration. Body jerk is a simulated finite-difference diagnostic, not measured mechanical jerk.
manipulations: First/second finite differences at 20 Hz; whole-trial RMS; no smoothing/prepended values.
sample_unit: n=9 whole-trial statistics per condition×method

title: Turn-only angular smoothness
caption_en: Turn-only angular smoothness, complementary to the whole-trial smoothness plots. Each dot is one trial's statistic on samples with |κ|>0.15 1/m and each black bar the mean of nine trials per method/plant. Columns distinguish command increment, command rate, and numerical body jerk with different physical units. Finite differences are formed on the original regularly sampled trajectory before phase restriction, using only the valid within-phase intervals specified in the metric exporter, rather than differencing across disjoint turn segments. No filtering is applied. The accuracy gain must be read together with its command/body smoothness tradeoff.
manipulations: Use exported turn-only finite-difference RMS metrics; descriptive mean; no smoothing.

title: Angular response/lag association, nominal
caption_en: Seed-0 S-bend angular-response diagnostic under the nominal plant. Upper row compares target-speed reference 0.20κ(s(t)), issued angular command, and simulated body response. Lower row gives overlap-normalized, demeaned Pearson correlations corr(reference(t), response(t+lag)) over −1 to +1 s on a 0.05 s grid. Command is timestamped at t−0.05 s; response interpolation is linear solely for lag alignment. Positive lag means response trails the reference. Correlation includes closed-loop coupling and path-progress dependence; it is an association diagnostic, not an identified physical delay or causal measurement.
manipulations: Command timestamp correction; target reference 0.20κ; per-lag overlap Pearson correlation; linear interpolation for alignment only.
sample_unit: One preselected S-bend trial per method; dependent time samples; no confidence intervals

title: Recovery from initial tracking offsets
caption_en: Initial-offset recovery in the left-turn supplementary test (initial lateral offset 0.10 m and heading offset +10 deg). All three seed traces per method/plant are overlaid, without temporal smoothing or pointwise confidence bands. Dashed lines show the predeclared 10 mm lateral and 2 deg heading bands; convergence requires joint continuous residence in both bands for the declared hold duration, not merely one threshold crossing. This empirical finite-run recovery is not a stability theorem.
manipulations: Absolute errors, SI→mm/deg; three raw seed traces, no envelope/CI or filter.
sample_unit: 24 supplementary closed-loop trials; three seeds per condition×method
font: DejaVu Sans; PDF embedded TrueType; SVG editable text
evidence: synthetic closed-loop simulation, not FAST-LIO/NDT execution

title: Joint-band settling and right censoring
caption_en: Joint-band settling times for every left-turn initial-offset recovery trial. Left: first continuous 1 s window within both 10 mm lateral and 2 deg heading bands. Right: time after the last observed threshold exit, accepted only when the terminal in-band dwell is at least 1 s. Filled circles denote observed events; open downward triangles denote right-censored trials at their own observation horizon. Horizons vary because trials end at geometric route completion or failure. Censored trials are neither assigned zero nor excluded. Labels c=n/N report the censored count. Last-exit settling is retrospective over a finite run, not a guarantee of future residence.
manipulations: Summary settling times; censored runs plotted at observation horizon with open triangles.
sample_unit: All 24 recovery attempts, including censored runs

title: Sampling diagnostics during offset recovery
caption_en: Available sampling diagnostics for both residual methods during all initial-offset recovery runs (three seeds per plant/method). Left: effective sample size divided by the 1000 sampled sequences. Right: minimum sampled cost (dotted) and selected sequence cost (solid). Only observations with diagnostics_available=1 and command_valid=1 are plotted; zero placeholders for unavailable native/tracker diagnostics are excluded. The horizon and measured state change every call, so the cost sequence is a receding-horizon diagnostic, not optimizer convergence across iterations and not an inter-method optimality test. Costs are in arbitrary units and no temporal smoothing is used.
manipulations: Mask unavailable diagnostics/commands; ESS divided by 1000; raw receding-horizon costs, no filter.
sample_unit: 12 supplementary residual-controller runs; three seeds per plant/method
